name: Alpha-thalassemia-myelodysplastic syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for Alpha-thalassemia-myelodysplastic syndrome

criteria.description: Molecular confirmation of alpha-globin gene deletions or mutations consistent with alpha-thalassemia
Bone marrow biopsy showing dysplastic changes in one or more myeloid lineages with <20% blasts
Presence of persistent cytopenias (anemia, neutropenia, or thrombocytopenia) unexplained by other causes
Exclusion of other causes of cytopenias and myelodysplasia such as vitamin deficiencies, infections, or other hematologic malignancies
Hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC showing alpha-thalassemia related hemoglobin abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular confirmation of alpha-thalassemia plus bone marrow dysplasia with persistent cytopenias
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of hematological, genetic, and bone marrow findings to distinguish from isolated alpha-thalassemia or primary myelodysplastic syndromes.

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing microcytic hypochromic anemia with anisopoikilocytosis
Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating dysplastic changes in erythroid, myeloid, and megakaryocytic lineages
Hemoglobin electrophoresis revealing decreased alpha-globin chains and presence of HbH
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing splenomegaly and mild hepatomegaly
MRI may reveal extramedullary hematopoiesis in rare cases
other: Inclusion bodies (HbH) detected by supravital staining of erythrocytes
Elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) due to hemolysis

distinguishingFeatures: Mild anemia without cytopenias in other lineages
Beta-globin gene mutations instead of alpha-globin

redFlags: Development of blasts >20% indicating acute leukemia transformation
Severe bleeding or infections due to marrow failure
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Higgs DR, et al. The molecular basis of alpha-thalassemia. Cold Spring Harb Perspect Med. 2012.
